title: Respond to interview advice
prompt: Write two short comments responding to advice about preparing for a job interview. Appreciate one useful idea and politely disagree with another. Give reasons for both.
checks: I expressed agreement or disagreement politely.
I checked tense and verb choices.

title: A food trend opinion
prompt: Write about a food trend you have noticed. Explain why it attracts people and what may happen if it continues. Use because, so and a real conditional. Present opinions as opinions.
checks: I separated my opinions from facts.

title: A shopping experience
prompt: Describe a shopping experience that went wrong. Explain what happened first, what the problem was and how people responded. Use linking words and a comparison.
checks: I gave events in a clear order.

title: Support an opinion with examples
prompt: Write a short opinion about a brand that wants to enter a different market. Suggest why local knowledge matters and give two invented examples. Use for example or such as.

title: Write a clear apology
prompt: Write an apology for missing an arrangement with a friend. Explain what had happened, take responsibility and offer a way to put it right. Choose a suitable informal register.
checks: I stated what I was apologizing for.

title: A community proposal
prompt: Propose an improvement to a public space. Explain what should be done, who could help and how the result would benefit people. Use passive forms where useful.

title: Compare communication opinions
prompt: Compare two opinions about using emojis in class or at work. State where the people agree and disagree, then give your view. Use reported statements and contrast words.

title: An imagined lifestyle change
prompt: Describe a change that would improve your work/life balance. Explain what you would do if you had the opportunity and one thing you wish were different now.

title: Summarize contrasting arguments
prompt: Summarize two contrasting views about a community rule or accessibility service. Attribute each view to its speaker, explain the reasons and state your own view respectfully.
checks: I attributed claims to their speakers.
I avoided treating one speaker's claims as established facts.

title: What I could live without
prompt: Describe a possession or service you once considered essential. Explain what life might have been like without it and what matters more to you now. Use a past unreal conditional.
checks: I used a past unreal conditional.
I gave reasons for my current view.

title: An opinion with ordered arguments
prompt: Write a short opinion about a new technology. Begin with your position, add two supporting arguments and conclude. Use expressions such as first of all, in addition and all in all.

title: A balanced opinion summary
prompt: Summarize two opinions about pet training or another everyday issue. Describe the supporting examples and compare the arguments using while, although or despite. Then give a brief conclusion.
